l8hu-exploitative: HU Exploitation: Not Abandoning GTO, Calibrating It

HU exploitative play profits from the opponent's deviations from equilibrium. But HU pros don't "abandon" GTO; they "calibrate" it: using equilibrium frequencies as the baseline and making minimum necessary deviations against the opponent's clear deviations. HU is the format where reading people is most valuable — facing one opponent, you can quickly identify his leaks and harvest with targeted strategies.

The right posture of exploitation: aim the direction at the opponent's leak (Maximally Exploitative), keep the magnitude minimal (Minimally Exploitative). Every deviation opens your own leaks, so keep the magnitude controlled and return to baseline when the opponent adjusts.
Frequency Reading: From Statistics to Exploitation

Frequency reading is the foundation of HU exploitation: identify the opponent's four-dimensional tendencies (open rate, fold rate vs C-Bets, 3-bet rate, showdown tendency), then harvest with targeted strategies. Folds too much → raise C-Bet/steal frequency; calls too loose (station) → value-bet thin value and cut pure bluffs; 3-bets too often → narrow the open and add 4Bet; C-Bets too often → raise x/r. Identification relies on 50-100 hand statistics; single-hand impressions don't count.

Example: You observe a HU opponent who folds to C-Bets at 62% (equilibrium ~45%). That's a clear over-folding leak. Exploit: raise your flop C-Bet frequency and bluff density overall, even adding weak hands that originally checked to the betting range. But cap it at "I still don't lose if he tightens to 50%" — keeping correction room. That's a "directed, disciplined deviation".

Example 2 (range polarization): Against a station who calls too loose, polarize your betting range — bet value with the nuts, semi-bluff with strong draws, check middle hands. Because the station calls with weak hands, your wide value range gets overpaid. Meanwhile cut pure bluffs (he doesn't fold) and convert bluffs to semi-bluffs or checks.

Example 3 (dynamic adjustment): After you raise steal frequency, the opponent starts 3-betting frequently — he's discovered your deviation. Now you must return to the GTO baseline (narrow the steal range, reduce pure bluffs), or your newly opened leaks get harvested in reverse. Exploitation is a dynamic game: deviate → get detected → return to baseline, looping.

Counterintuitive point: the biggest risk of exploitation isn't "exploiting too little" but "over-exploiting and becoming the leak yourself". HU pros always keep one hand on the GTO baseline wheel while harvesting — the moment the opponent adjusts, they snap back.

Exploitation execution in five steps: (1) HUD-collect enough samples to confirm the leak; (2) lock the node in a solver for the optimal response; (3) compare to baseline and mark the pushed-up frequencies and sizes; (4) execute live; (5) re-check the sample every 500 hands. A "lock" without data support is exploitation on paper.

The marginal gain of exploitation must price EV and noise together (P = pot, b = bet size, f = fold rate, p = observed frequency, n = sample size):
One-street EV = f × P − (1 − f) × b
Frequency standard error = √(p(1−p)/n)

The same 1/3-pot C-Bet (P = 4BB, b = 1.33BB):
Equilibrium f = 45%: EV = 0.45×4 − 0.55×1.33 = 1.80 − 0.73 ≈ +1.07BB
Opponent f = 62%: EV = 0.62×4 − 0.38×1.33 = 2.48 − 0.51 ≈ +1.97BB
Marginal +0.90BB — that is where the deviation direction comes from.

Significance: with p = 0.62 the standard error is √(0.62×0.38/100) ≈ 4.9 percentage points over 100 hands and ≈ 10.9 percentage points over 20 hands.
The 17-point gap between 62% and 45% is about 3.5 standard errors over 100 hands (deviate) but only about 1.6 over 20 hands (hold still).

How to read it: the EV sign gives the direction, the standard error gives the magnitude cap — only when both clear the bar does the deviation go into your strategy.

Theory support: when to tighten or widen and when you must return to baseline is Theory Academy T7 "Targeted Adjustments" — that chapter turns "observe the deviation → capped adjustment → roll back when countered" into an executable order, and this lesson's five-step loop is its strategy-side application.

Theory support: the open rate, fold-to-C-Bet and 3-bet rate cited here, with their definitions and HU baselines, are Theory Academy T7 "Heads-Up Match Metrics" — that chapter gives each metric's definition and sample-size requirement, and underpins the rule that "62% is a deviation while 35% is noise".

HU exploitation in three lines:
Use equilibrium as the baseline — aim the direction at the leak, cap the magnitude, and demand enough evidence
Folds too much → bet and bluff more; calls too much → bluff less and widen the value range with thin value bets
Once the opponent's frequencies change, return to baseline — exploitation is a "deviate, get detected, reset" loop, not a one-time setting

l8hu-exploitative-q1.question: The correct basis of HU exploitation is:
options: Using GTO as the baseline and making minimum necessary deviations against clear opponent deviations
l8hu-exploitative-q1.explanation: Exploitation is "calibrating GTO" rather than abandoning it: using equilibrium frequencies as the baseline and making directed, capped deviations against opponent deviations.

l8hu-exploitative-q2.question: Against an over-folding opponent, HU exploitation is:
options: Raise C-Bet/steal frequency and bluff density
l8hu-exploitative-q2.explanation: An over-folding opponent makes steal and C-Bet fold rates automatic profit — raise C-Bet/steal frequency and bluff density.

l8hu-exploitative-q3.question: Against a station who calls too loose, the correct exploitation is:
options: Polarize the betting range, value-bet thin value, cut pure bluffs
l8hu-exploitative-q3.explanation: A station calls with weak hands so thin value bets get overpaid; pure bluffs are useless (he doesn't fold) — convert to semi-bluffs or checks.

l8hu-exploitative-q4.question: After you raise steals, the opponent starts 3-betting frequently. The correct move is:
options: Return to the GTO baseline and narrow the range
l8hu-exploitative-q4.explanation: The opponent detected your deviation and your newly opened leaks will be harvested in reverse — you must return to baseline. Exploitation is a "deviate → get detected → return" dynamic game.

l8hu-exploitative-q5.question: HU exploitation's frequency reading relies on:
l8hu-exploitative-q5.explanation: Frequency reading relies on 50-100 hand statistics (open rate/fold rate/3-bet rate/showdown tendency); single-hand impressions are noise.

l8hu-exploitative-q6.question: The pot is 4BB and you bet 1.33BB (1/3 pot) on the flop. The opponent folds to C-Bets 62% of the time (equilibrium about 45%). The exploitative EV of this street is about:
l8hu-exploitative-q6.explanation: EV = f×P − (1−f)×b = 0.62×4 − 0.38×1.33 = 2.48 − 0.51 ≈ +1.97BB. +2.48 counts only the fold gain and drops the 0.51 lost when called; +1.07 is the EV at the equilibrium 45% fold rate (0.45×4 − 0.55×1.33); −0.51 flips the signs of both branches.

l8hu-exploitative-q7.question: In a 100-hand sample the opponent folds to C-Bets 62 times. The standard error of this frequency is about:
l8hu-exploitative-q7.explanation: Frequency standard error = √(p(1−p)/n) = √(0.62×0.38/100) = √0.002356 ≈ 0.0485, i.e. about 4.9 percentage points. Quadrupling the sample only halves it; 17 points is the gap between 62% and 45%, not the noise scale; 0.6 points treats the denominator as 10000.

l8hu-exploitative-q8.question: With only a 20-hand sample you see the opponent fold 62% (baseline 45%). By significance testing the correct action is:
options: Double the C-Bet frequency right away
Keep sampling and hold off on deviating
l8hu-exploitative-q8.explanation: Over 20 hands the standard error is √(0.62×0.38/20) ≈ 10.9 percentage points, so the 17-point gap is only about 1.6 standard errors — short of the 2-standard-error bar, and the observation may still be noise. The correct move is to gather more sample first; deviating hard on thin data turns you into the opponent's exploitation target.

l8hu-exploitative-q9.question: A sound HU exploitative adjustment must have all of:
options: Direction, a magnitude cap and sample evidence
l8hu-exploitative-q9.explanation: All three gates are mandatory: direction (which way to deviate), magnitude (how far, measured as a frequency gap rather than a feeling) and evidence (whether the sample supports that direction). No direction is random play; no magnitude cap becomes a new leak once the opponent adjusts; no evidence is just "I think he folds a lot".

l8hu-exploitative-q10.question: At the same node, opponent A folds to C-Bets 62% while opponent B folds only 30%. Your betting-range adjustment should be:
options: Raise bluff density against A; cut bluffs and widen the value range against B
Cut bluffs against A and raise them against B
l8hu-exploitative-q10.explanation: The exploitation direction follows the direction of the deviation: A over-folds → the fold rate pays you, so raise bluff density and betting frequency; B over-calls → pure bluffs stop working, so cut bluffs, widen the value range and add thin value bets. The two directions are opposite — using one set of frequencies against both simply gives away the exploit.

l8hu-exploitative-ex2.title: Polarizing against a station: top pair bets big, not small
reasoning: The opponent's WTSD is high and he folds to C-Bets only 30%: he habitually calls with weak pairs and draws, so a small bet buys no fold equity
KQ on Q-8-4 is top pair good kicker — the top of the value range against a station, so the sizing should grow, not shrink
75% pot charges his 8x, 4x and backdoor draws; the other pole of the range semi-bluffs strong draws, and pure bluffs shrink because he does not fold
l8hu-exploitative-ex2.mistakeReasoning: That imports the small-bet template onto a station: with only a 30% fold rate a 1/3-pot bet buys no folds and collects too little value across three streets.

l8hu-exploitative-ex3.title: The opponent starts 3-betting back: reset to baseline instead of stealing harder
reasoning: The BB's 3-bet rate climbs from the ~10% baseline to 20% — the classic "I've been detected" signal: frequency change is the signal, results are not
The fold rate slides to about 30%, below the 50% break-even line a min-raise needs (1.5 ÷ 3): EV = 0.3 × 1.5 − 0.7 × 1.5 = −0.6BB
Resetting means three things: narrow the opening range, move J9s-type marginal suited connectors out of the open, and cut pure bluffs until the 3-bet rate falls back to 10%-12% before deviating again
l8hu-exploitative-ex3.mistakeReasoning: Running a fixed steal frequency against an opponent who has already countered turns your deviation into his free profit.
